open_points.subject: AuditEntry sequence number after backup restoration
open_points.text: “never reused, also after old entries are erased” conflicts with “A store restored from a backup continues the backup's history, whose last number it continues from” when entries had been written after that backup.
open_points.question: After restoring an older backup, may Registry reuse sequence numbers that were assigned to post-backup entries before the restore?
options: Sequence numbers are never reused across the instance's real execution history, so a high-water mark outside the restored backup must survive.
The restored backup defines the continuing history, so numbers assigned only after that backup may be assigned again to different entries.
open_points.default_guess: The restored backup defines the continuing history, so Registry continues from its last number and may reuse numbers from the discarded post-backup history.

open_points.subject: One-time import after restoring a pre-import backup
open_points.text: “A store restored from a backup made before the import continues that backup's history, in which it is absent” conflicts with State 0's “after the first successful import the operation is closed and refused” and “The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once.”
open_points.question: If the import succeeded and the store is later restored from a backup made before it, is another import permitted or must the prior real-world success still keep the operation closed?
options: The successful import closes the operation permanently across restores, so its closure must survive outside a pre-import backup.
Restoring a pre-import backup removes the closure from the continuing store history and permits the import to succeed again.
open_points.default_guess: Restoring the pre-import backup permits the import again, following the new explicit lifecycle sentence.
